For a function \(\pi :A\to A\) that is onto a finite set, \(\pi\) must be a bijection; i.e. \(\pi\) is a permutation of the six elements.

The condition  

\[
\pi(\pi(\pi(\pi(\pi(\pi(a)))))) = a\qquad\forall a\in A
\]

means that \(\pi^{6}\) is the identity permutation.  
If a permutation \(\sigma\) has order \(d\) (the smallest positive integer with \(\sigma^{d}=id\)), then \(\sigma^{6}=id\) iff \(d\mid 6\).
Hence we must count all permutations of \(S_{6}\) whose order is \(1,2,3\) or \(6\).

---

### 1. Order \(1\) – the identity  

\[
\# =1
\]

### 2. Order \(2\) – involutions  

Involutions are products of disjoint transpositions.  
The possible cycle types are \((2),\;(2,2),\;(2,2,2)\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
(2)&:\ \binom{6}{2}=15,\\[2pt]
(2,2)&:\ \frac{\binom{6}{2}\binom{4}{2}}{2}=45,\\[2pt]
(2,2,2)&:\ (6-1)!! =15.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus \(\#_{2}=15+45+15=75\).

### 3. Order \(3\)  

The cycle types giving order \(3\) are \((3)\) and \((3,3)\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
(3)&:\ \binom{6}{3}\,(3-1)! =20\cdot2 =40,\\[2pt]
(3,3)&:\ \frac{\binom{6}{3}}{2}\,(3-1)!^{2}=10\cdot4 =40.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence \(\#_{3}=40+40=80\).

### 4. Order \(6\)  

The only cycle types with l.c.m. \(=6\) are \((6)\) and \((3,2)\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
(6)&:\ (6-1)! =5! =120,\\[2pt]
(3,2)&:\ \frac{6!}{3^{1}2^{1}} =\frac{720}{6}=120.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus \(\#_{6}=120+120=240\).

---

Adding all admissible permutations:

\[
1\;(\text{order }1)+\;75\;(\text{order }2)+\;80\;(\text{order }3)+\;240\;(\text{order }6)=396.
\]

Therefore the number of functions \(\pi\) satisfying the given condition is  

\[
\boxed{396}.
\]
